title: Three Lines of Defence and Operational Risk Governance

maps.tested: Reported as a named topic in two sittings. Always won or lost on who does what, not on what is done: the role-misassignment operator in its purest form.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'three lines of Operational Risk Management'; 'Ops Risk Level 3 categorisation': the Basel event-type taxonomy at its third level, a separate recall item. Business lines own risk (first line); the risk function sets framework and challenges (second); internal audit provides independent assurance (third). Any statement moving an activity across those boundaries is the defect.

vardeezReading: ORR-2: untiered, "use crash course notes for ORR-1 to ORR-9; no Schweser needed". CR-2: Not So Important, "Again Not much expected here. Just Read this Carefully" (the key principles of credit risk governance: Guidelines, Skills, Limits, Oversight). ORR-1: untiered, "use crash course notes for ORR-1 to ORR-9; no Schweser needed". ORR-3: untiered, "use crash course notes for ORR-1 to ORR-9; no Schweser needed".

selectors.name: Three lines: who does what
selectors.what: Who owns and who does what in the three lines of operational risk management: risk owners in the business (line 1, with risk champions at 1.5), the independent corporate risk function (line 2, owns the methodology, challenges, may veto), internal audit (line 3, independent assurance). Each wrong option moves an activity across a line, for example the risk function owning the risk, the first line not signing off its own assessment, or internal audit relying only on the risk function's testing.

selectors.name: Basel event-type taxonomy, Levels 1 to 3
selectors.what: Classify an operational loss event into the seven Basel Level 1 event types and their Level 2 categories, or recognise the Level 3 examples that discriminate (insider trading on or not on the firm's account, check kiting by internal or external party, model error versus model misoperation, utility outage, hacking). Level 3 gives examples only; the regulatory categories are Levels 1 and 2.

selectors.name: Board, committees, risk appetite ownership
selectors.what: Who does what among the board, the board risk committee, the executive and group operational risk committees and senior management: the board is ultimately responsible, approves the framework and the risk appetite statement and owns the limits, committees escalate upward and recommend, senior management implements. Also what makes a risk appetite statement and a risk culture sound.

notSelected: ORR-2 a (Basel regulatory expectations: Pillar 1, 2 and 3 treatment and the principles of the RPSMOR) and ORR-3 c (taxonomies in general, such as the ORX reference taxonomy) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer, and the credit governance parts of CR-2 (b to e) are outside this topic.
